events.title: S&P cuts Oracle to BBB- (one notch above junk)
events.detail: S&P lowered Oracle's long-term issuer rating to BBB- from BBB, citing AI data-center cash burn (FY ended May 31 free cash flow roughly -$24B; S&P sees deficit possibly widening to $42B; adjusted leverage above 4x). Moody's outlook negative per Bloomberg Tax; Fitch BBB per Reuters/Euronext. Shares fell nearly 6% that day. Oracle says holding investment grade is a top priority. Dates differ slightly across outlets (Bloomberg Law dated Jul 16).
events.why_it_matters: A rating agency explicitly linking AI-capex funding to credit quality. Another notch would put Oracle bonds at risk of index exclusion.

events.title: Axios: Nvidia weighs financing guarantee for OpenAI Ohio campus, reigniting 'circular' concerns
events.detail: Late-July reports said Nvidia was considering a guarantee for an OpenAI data-center campus in southern Ohio. Some outlets cited $250B; later reporting settled on $105B. Headline figure was inconsistent across sources. (Axios page returned 403 to the fetcher; headline seen in search results only.)
events.why_it_matters: Marks the shift from equity investment to contingent credit support by the chip supplier.

events.title: Nvidia agrees to guarantee up to $105B of OpenAI Ohio lease payments (SB Energy campus)
events.detail: Reuters (via Investing.com/Nikkei) reported Nvidia would guarantee up to $105B in lease payments for an OpenAI data center being built by SoftBank-backed SB Energy, invest $1.5B in SB Energy, and secure up to 8 GW of capacity. Per Data Center Knowledge the guarantee is a conditional ceiling tied to residual value of leased infrastructure, not a cash outlay; Nvidia says it has not paid under any guarantee. A Substack (low reliability) says total guarantees later rose to $118.0B from $108.5B; unconfirmed. Burry publicly called it a circular-financing red flag.
events.why_it_matters: The largest contingent liability in the AI financing web sits with the chip supplier, backing a customer that lacks an investment-grade rating. Bulls note it is conditional, building-by-building and not yet drawn.

events.title: Fed raises rates 25 bp to 3.75%-4.00%, first hike since 2023
events.detail: Per Yahoo/Motley Fool coverage. The October meeting held rates at 3.75%-4% on a 10-2 vote (Cook and Hammack dissenting for a hike); minutes show almost all participants see further hikes as likely appropriate.
events.why_it_matters: Higher funding costs for debt-financed buildouts; rate backdrop turned from easing to tightening.

events.title: Oracle sends force majeure notice on Project Jupiter (New Mexico Stargate campus)
events.detail: Oracle notified the developer (most outlets: a Blue Owl unit; one says STACK Infrastructure) that it reserves the right to delay payments if the site misses its 2028 target, amid air-permit and pipeline-reroute delays. Reports say Oracle is not exiting as tenant. Oracle stock fell ~3%. Reported that the project's $18B construction loan traded below 90 cents and county officials warned of possible breach of industrial revenue bond agreements (weakest-sourced part).
events.why_it_matters: First prominent case of a hyperscaler tenant invoking a contract clause on an AI campus financed by project debt. Not a missed payment or cancellation.

events.title: Oracle 5-yr CDS reaches record (reported ~288 bp)
events.detail: One source reports a record 288 bp on Oct 15; a Bloomberg-sourced report cites ~151 bp in early October; CNBC (Nov 6 and Nov 18) puts Oracle near 298 bp then 'above 300', up from below 80 a year earlier. Levels do not reconcile across sources and likely reflect different dates/quotes.
events.why_it_matters: Market pricing of Oracle credit risk at post-2009 highs while still rated investment grade.

events.title: Banks struggle to distribute ~$38B of construction debt tied to Oracle-leased Texas/Wisconsin data centers
events.detail: Search summary: a group including JPMorgan and MUFG spent more than six months trying to place the debt. Only seen in search-result summaries; primary article not fetched.
events.why_it_matters: Signals limited investor appetite for project-level data-center debt.

events.title: Hyperscaler Q3 earnings: combined free cash flow negative; no capex cuts
events.detail: Alphabet reaffirmed 2026 capex $195-205B and said 2027 will rise significantly; Amazon held ~$220B for 2026 and signalled 'meaningfully more' in 2027; Meta narrowed 2026 to $135-145B; Microsoft trimmed calendar 2026 to ~$170B and stayed FCF-positive. Goldman: hyperscalers' Q3 FCF negative as capex exceeded operating cash flow. Figures come from search summaries/Substack; check filings.
events.why_it_matters: Demand-side capex guidance is the base of the whole chain; the only trim was Microsoft, others are rising and increasingly debt funded.

events.title: CoreWeave 5-yr CDS spikes above 1,289 bp; bond yields exceed 16%
events.detail: Per Deutsche Bank via CNBC: CDS above 1,289 bp on Nov 5, ~1,155 on Nov 6 (Nvidia ~139, Oracle ~298). CoreWeave's high-yield bond yields above 16% (CNBC Nov 6 says 9.625% 2032 notes; Nov 18 says 9.75% 2031 notes; coupon/maturity differ between CNBC stories). Goldman counts five AI bond deals totalling $67B since Oct 29, $296B hyperscaler issuance in 2026, forecasts $440B hyperscaler plus $300B project issuance next year; BofA sees AI credit issuance peaking at $685B in 2027. Drivers cited: data-center moratorium risk after Democratic election wins (Goldman: could affect 45% of planned U.S. capacity), negative hyperscaler FCF. Jefferies' Christopher Wood: AI capex race ends when 'the credit card will be taken away'.
events.why_it_matters: Distress-level pricing on the most levered neocloud while issuance by hyperscalers is at record levels.

events.title: CoreWeave Q3: revenue +168%, backlog ~$132.5B, 2026 guidance raised; will avoid unsecured bonds at current yields
events.detail: Revenue ~$3.66B; adjusted operating income $379M; GAAP (standard US accounting) net loss $709M; interest expense $846M vs $310M a year earlier; 2026 capex guided $37-39B; backlog ~$132.5B (about $104B in June). Management said it will not use the unsecured bond market at current yields and expects to finance via delayed-draw term loans tied to customer contracts. Co-founder Brian Venturo says he bought $30M of unsecured bonds (CNBC Nov 18).
events.why_it_matters: Operating demand is strong (bull evidence) while financing cost and net losses are the stress point (bear evidence). Shut of unsecured market shifts reliance to contract-backed secured loans.

events.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO, president and director; CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO
events.detail: Nvidia 8-K says Kress is interim CEO while remaining CFO; board considering internal and external candidates. No reason given in the filing; media reports of personal conduct allegations are unconfirmed and are not repeated here as fact. Board accepted resignation Nov 11. Nvidia shares reportedly fell more than 10% initially; Nebius -16.8%, CoreWeave -6.9%, Super Micro -11.3% per a machine-translated Korean report (treat magnitudes as approximate). On the Nov 17 earnings call board chair Harvey Jones said the board does not intend to reinstate Huang. House committees to interview Huang Dec 1; Senate Banking Chair Tim Scott says Huang and Lutnick agreed to appear in December.
events.why_it_matters: Removes the figure most associated with Nvidia's ecosystem investments right as scrutiny of those deals peaks. Rowan and others argue Nvidia is the 'bank' for neoclouds, so leadership and strategy continuity matter for that financing. Cause and policy consequences are unknown.

events.title: Nebius trims 2026 revenue outlook on capacity delays; capex to ~$27B
events.detail: Revenue to low end of $3.0-3.4B range as third-party capacity slips to 1H27; 2026 capex ~$27B vs prior $20-25B; Q3 revenue $980.8M beat. Stock fell between ~12% and 22% depending on outlet and time of measurement.
events.why_it_matters: Delivery/power delays hit neocloud revenue timing while capex rises, widening the financing gap.

events.title: IMF chief reportedly says AI circular financing exceeds $1 trillion
events.detail: Invezz reports the IMF head said circular AI financing has crossed $1T, about two-thirds debt funded, and cites the IMF's October GFSR on 'wrong-way risk'. Invezz page was not fetchable (403) and the IMF primary document was not checked; a BIS warning is also mentioned in search summaries without primary verification.
events.why_it_matters: If accurate, a multilateral regulator is naming circular financing as a stability risk.

events.title: Nvidia Q3 FY2027: revenue $115.8B (+103% y/y); Q4 guide $130B; Rubin ships; stock falls
events.detail: Quarter ended Oct 25, 2026. Data Center $107.6B; GAAP (standard US accounting) net income $65.3B; GAAP gross margin 74.8%; Q4 guide $130B +/-3% (includes an extra week; gross margin guide 71-72%) with no China data-center compute revenue assumed. Consensus ~$109.1B revenue and ~$125.1B guide (LSEG via CNBC). Balance sheet: non-marketable securities $65.5B (from $22.3B), marketable equity securities $44.2B (from $12.9B), long-term debt $32.4B (from $7.5B); new $150B buyback authorization; pending Hugging Face acquisition. Stock closed -2.89% at $150.96 on Nov 18 and is down >13% over the week; reported 36-39% below its October high (sources differ). CoreWeave -4.13%, Iren -3.61% on Nov 18.
events.why_it_matters: Operating results are very strong, but Nvidia's own balance sheet shows rapid growth in equity stakes and debt, which is the heart of the circularity debate. The release gives no dollar figure for guarantees.

events.title: Fed October minutes: staff warn off-balance-sheet leasing and circular financing could amplify AI losses
events.detail: Minutes (released Nov 18) say officials see AI demand as a material inflation risk and a possible source of financial instability; staff warned that 'off-balance-sheet leasing commitments and circular financing arrangements among AI-related firms could amplify losses' if returns disappoint; most participants noted rapid, opaque growth in AI-related debt.
events.why_it_matters: First clear central-bank wording on circular financing in primary Fed communication (as relayed by CNBC).

events.title: Defiance and Tuttle file for CDS-based ETFs on Oracle, CoreWeave, Meta and Mag 7
events.detail: Funds need SEC approval; would pay CDS premiums and use leverage; not inverse-stock products. Same CNBC piece: Apollo CEO Marc Rowan (Nov 17) warned neoclouds could lose access to capital if Nvidia's role as funder fades.
events.why_it_matters: Retail/institutional access to AI credit hedges is a sentiment indicator, not evidence of default.

events.title: Neocloud and AI-credit equities deeply below peaks
events.detail: CoreWeave closed $44.91 on Nov 19 (reported), about 76% below the $183.58 peak (Jun 2025), close to its $40 IPO price. A Kobeissi-based list puts Oracle ~68% below its high (unverified list). Nvidia reported 36-39% below its October high.
events.why_it_matters: Equity and credit markets are pricing financing risk, though CoreWeave's operating metrics still grow.

events.title: No confirmed public default on a GPU-backed loan found
events.detail: A vendor tracker (AM Compute) says no neocloud had publicly defaulted on a GPU-backed loan as of October 2026. My searches also found no confirmed missed payment, covenant breach disclosure or confirmed cancellation of the OpenAI-Oracle contract; Oracle has denied delays that would breach contractual commitments (earlier DCD report).
events.why_it_matters: Stress so far is in prices and spreads, not realized credit losses (Lucent's defaults came in 2001, about a year after peak financing).

bull_arguments.claim: Nvidia's exposure is conditional and small relative to cash generation: guarantees are a ceiling tied to residual value, undrawn, and Nvidia has paid nothing; Q3 net income was $65.3B and FCF is large. Lucent financed customers from a far weaker cash position.
bull_arguments.who: Nvidia disclosures and analysts such as UBS (exposure up to ~13% of 2026E revenue); Data Center Knowledge on guarantee structure

bull_arguments.claim: Demand is real and backlogged: Nvidia revenue +103% y/y with Rubin shipping; CoreWeave backlog ~$132.5B with 2026 guidance raised; interim CEO Kress says hyperscalers are looking for more compute; H100 rental rates rising (Huang, Sept).
bull_arguments.who: Nvidia (Colette Kress); CoreWeave management; Jensen Huang (Sept 2026)

bull_arguments.claim: Buyers are the richest firms on earth with operating cash flow, unlike dot-com startups; policymakers expect build-out to continue (NEC's Kevin Hassett); a 25-50 bp tightening alone would not end the build-out.
bull_arguments.who: Kevin Hassett (NEC); sell-side commentary summarized by Yahoo Finance

bull_arguments.claim: Rating and credit stress shows up in a small set of levered names; Nvidia's CDS (~139 bp) is far below Oracle's and CoreWeave's, and no public GPU-loan default has occurred.
bull_arguments.who: CNBC/Deutsche Bank spread data; AM Compute tracker

bull_arguments.claim: Jensen Huang's public stance: 'circular financing' fears are overstated ('If that is, let's do more of that').

bear_arguments.claim: Circular flows inflate reported demand: Nvidia funds or backstops customers (OpenAI guarantee up to $105B, equity stakes, unsold-capacity purchase commitments) who buy its chips, and the guarantee depends on an OpenAI lacking investment-grade credit.
Neoclouds depend on Nvidia as 'the bank'; if that support fades many would lose access to capital.
Fed staff: off-balance-sheet leasing and circular financing could amplify losses if AI returns disappoint; AI debt grew fast through opaque structures.
The AI capex race will end when credit is withdrawn; hyperscaler FCF has turned negative and debt issuance is surging ($296B in 2026, $440B plus $300B projected).

GPU useful lives are overstated in depreciation schedules (Burry estimate ~$176B understated depreciation 2026-2028), so collateral is shorter-lived than long-haul fiber was. Chanos questioned why chip owners do not rent chips out themselves.

The Lucent/Nortel parallel: vendor lent to or guaranteed customers who later failed; concentrated customers, rising contingent commitments and a leadership shock are the bear framing (framing, not a tested conclusion).
bear_arguments.who: Commentators such as Tomasz Tunguz; Bernstein's Stacy Rasgon on circular concerns
